title: Food Preference Assay of C. elegans
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yb5fsq6

steps.title: Prepare OP50 and HB101 cultures
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh bacterial cultures of OP50 and HB101 following the “Making OP50 solution from Frozen Stock” protocol (by Priota Islam).

steps.title: Maintain and synchronize N2 worms
steps.instruction: Maintain N2 worms on NGM plates seeded with OP50, HB101, or a mixture as required. Chunk each set onto three maintenance plates. After 2 days, bleach‑synchronize the worms using the Bleach synchronization protocol (https://www.protocols.io/view/bleach-synchronisation-of-c-elegans-stbeein). Refeed the starved L1 larvae onto two plates seeded with OP50, HB101, or a mixture, 72 h before the experiment day.

substeps.instruction: Maintain worms on seeded NGM plates.
Chunk each set onto three maintenance plates.
Bleach‑synchronize after 2 days using the referenced protocol.
Refeed starved L1s onto two plates with the appropriate bacterial seed 72 h before the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare low‑peptone imaging plates
steps.instruction: Pour low‑peptone NGM agar onto 35 mm imaging plates and store them in a cold room for at least 2 days before use. Dilute OP50 and HB101 in M9 to the desired dilution factor (1:1, 1:2, 1:4, 1:8, or 1:10). Label each plate according to the experiment plan, using two dots for OP50 and one dot for HB101 spaced ~1.5 cm apart. Seed each plate with two 10 µL drops of the appropriate diluted bacterial suspension the day before recording (control plates receive two drops of a single strain; experimental plates receive one drop of each strain). Leave plates on the bench, lids on, to dry overnight.

substeps.instruction: Pour low‑peptone NGM onto 35 mm plates.
Store plates in a cold room for ≥2 days.
Dilute OP50 and HB101 in M9 to the chosen dilution factor.
Label plates (two dots for OP50, one dot for HB101, ~1.5 cm apart).
Seed plates with two 10 µL drops of diluted bacteria the day before recording.
Leave plates on bench with lids on to dry overnight.

steps.title: Place worms and record behavior
steps.instruction: Using a hair pick, transfer three young adult worms onto each seeded imaging plate. Place the plates on the multi‑worm tracker agar side up, lids off. Allow worms to acclimatize for 30 min, then record video for 2 h following the “Imaging on the multiworm tracker” protocol (by Priota Islam).

substeps.instruction: Pick 3 young adult worms onto each seeded plate with a hair pick.
Put plates on the tracker agar side up, lids off.
Record for 2 h using the multi‑worm tracker protocol.
